A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same risk-monitoring framework, with matching authors, core methods and experiments. The complete main texts, figures, equations and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original risk-monitoring experiments on ImageNet-C, Yearbook and FMoW-Time, including baseline comparisons, collapse detection and proxy/calibration ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds entropy-proxy, calibration-frequency and Yearbook label-shift results.

M1.justification: The core alarms and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. Appendices A.2–A.3 add an entropy-proxy instantiation and a tested periodic-calibration variant that reuses thresholds between calibration steps; less frequent calibration was only future work in v1.

E1.justification: The three datasets and classification tasks remain unchanged. v2 adds a Yearbook test scenario with temporally shifting label distributions, constructed by class-label reordering (Appendix A.5).

E2.justification: The proxy comparison gains predictive entropy alongside uncertainty and energy: v1 Figure 7 becomes v2 Figure 6. The supervised oracle, naive plug-in and Amoukou et al. monitoring baselines remain unchanged. SHOT was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: New protocols test calibration every 1, 2, 5, 10 or 20 adaptation steps and compare ordinary versus class-reordered Yearbook streams. Existing dataset splits, architectures, batch sizes, monitored losses and risk-control settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary validation: it tests entropy as both adaptation objective and monitoring proxy, sensitivity to calibration frequency, and robustness to label-shift-induced failures (Appendices A.2, A.3 and A.5). These address distinct questions beyond v1's retained proxy, calibration-size and collapse analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations, normally over 20 runs. Appendix D.3 changes the 10-seed exceptions from v1 Figures 5 and 8 to v2 Figures 4 and 5. Matching experiments therefore changes the stated collapse count from 20 to 10 and calibration-size count from 10 to 20. Their unchanged plots do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result sets showing broadly comparable entropy-proxy detection delays, small detection-delay increases with less frequent calibration, and higher Yearbook risks with earlier alarms under label shift (Figures 6, 8 and 10). These are additional findings under added variants or conditions; retained benchmark, collapse, prototype-distance and calibration-size plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 corrects the declared loss-threshold domain from (0, C), where C is the class count, to (0, M), consistent with the loss bound in Proposition 1. Assumption 1, the propositions, corollary and proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: label-free monitoring of adapting models, statistical false-alarm control and detection of harmful shifts or collapse. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations that threshold recalibration permits entropy to serve simultaneously as adaptation objective and monitoring proxy, that periodic calibration offers an overhead/delay tradeoff, and that monitoring remains effective under label shift. Existing limitations concerning detection delay and label-dependent verification of Assumption 1 remain.

D1.justification: The new experiments document threshold reuse between periodic calibrations and construction of the label-shift stream by class-label reordering. Existing hardware, software package, batch-size, hyperparameter and code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds WATCH and expands discussion of the already-cited instantaneous-risk monitoring work by Timans et al. The UniTTA reference and its Appendix E citations are removed. Other publication and title updates, including the STAD reference, concern matched existing works.

P1.justification: Changes include local related-work restructuring, expanded Appendix A explanations, revised cross-references and replacement of the preprint footer with the NeurIPS conference notice. Most main-text prose and the theoretical and algorithmic appendices remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v1's full comparison including SHOT (Figure 6) becomes v2's main Figure 3, eliminating the separate appendix display. The proxy figure gains entropy curves, new Figures 8 and 10 present additional experiments, and Figure 1's labels are revised. Other plots retain their content, with localized placement changes.

improvement.justification: The calibration-frequency and label-shift experiments provide useful evidence for practical questions left untested in v1, while preserving the core framework and proofs. The gain is limited by inconsistent entropy reporting: Section 5.4 calls its bounds looser than uncertainty's, whereas Figure 6 often shows higher bounds and Appendix A.2 reports comparable detection delays.
